explain.say: A sailing boat cannot sail straight into the wind, but it can sail at an angle of about 45 degrees to it. By zigzagging, called tacking, it can make its way to a place directly upwind.

explain.say: With the sail set at a slight angle, wind flows round it like air over a wing. The curved sail makes a force pointing mostly sideways, but also a little forwards.

explain.say: Under the boat, a deep fin called the keel or centreboard grips the water. It resists being pushed sideways, cancelling most of the sideways part of the sail force.

explain.say: What is left is the small forward part, which drives the boat ahead against the drag of the water. When these forces balance, the boat sails steadily at an angle across the wind.

faq.q: How does a sail work like a wing?
faq.a: Wind flowing round the curved sail speeds up on the outer side, and the pressure there drops. The difference in pressure gives a force roughly at right angles to the sail, much like the lift on a wing.
asks: Is a sail like an aeroplane wing?

faq.a: The keel is a deep fin under the boat. Water resists it moving sideways, so it cancels the sideways push of the sail and lets the forward part move the boat ahead. Its weight also keeps the boat upright.
asks: Why do sailing boats have a keel?

faq.q: What slows a sailing boat down?
faq.a: Water drag on the hull and keel, and waves made by the boat, push back against its motion. Smooth, slim hulls reduce drag.
Tacking is zigzagging towards a place upwind. The boat sails at about 45 degrees to the wind on one side, then turns through the wind and sails at 45 degrees on the other.
asks: How do you sail against the wind?

faq.q: Why can't a boat sail straight into the wind?
faq.a: Pointing straight into the wind, the sail just flaps and makes no useful force. The sail needs the wind to meet it at an angle to work like a wing.
asks: What is the no-go zone in sailing?

facts: Most sailing boats can sail at about 40 to 45 degrees to the wind.
A sail makes force in the same way as a wing, by changing the speed and pressure of the air flowing round it.
Zigzagging towards a place upwind is called tacking or beating.

quiz.say: What stops a sailing boat being blown sideways when it sails across the wind?
quiz.show: What stops a sailing boat being blown sideways when it sails across the wind?
quiz.why: The keel resists sideways motion, leaving the forward part of the sail force to drive the boat.

wrong.1: The mast holds the sail up; it does not resist sideways movement through the water.
wrong.2: An anchor is only used when the boat is stopped.
